newsitem.title: FRANCE: C. Lyonnais sees positive impact of Asia unit sale.
newsitem.headline: C. Lyonnais sees positive impact of Asia unit sale.

text.p: French state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais said on Wednesday that the sale of its CLIAM-Asia unit to a U.S. fund management firm would help 1997 earnings but would not disclose by how much.

The sale of Credit Lyonnais International Asset Management-Asia (CLIAM-Asia) to Nicholas-Applegate would have a "positive impact on Credit Lyonnais accounts in 1997", the bank said in a statement. Neither party would reveal the price.
U.S.-based Nicholas-Applegate announced earlier on Wednesday it would buy CLIAM-Asia in what analysts said was another indication of industry consolidation in the region.
The deal, Nicholas-Applegate said, would improve its access to Asia while extending CLIAM-Asia's reach around the world.
Analysts said Nicholas-Applegate probably paid in the upper range of a usual band of 1.5 percent and three percent of total assets managed by the target firm, in this case $700 million.
That works out to about $21 million. Nicholas-Applegate, whose headquarters are in San Diego, manages total assets of $30 billion.

Credit Lyonnais, rescued by the French government from collapse after an ill-fated lending spree, has been disposing of non-French assets to meet conditions set by the European Commission for approving state aid for the bank.
Once the world's largest bank outside Japan, the bank plans to limit its retail banking activities to France and focus on wholesale banking and capital market operations internationally.
A bank spokesman denied speculation in Hong Kong that the deal might mean Credit Lyonnais could divest its successful brokerage in Hong Kong.
"Credit Lyonnais Securities will remain in our portfolio. It is a strategic holding. There's no question of selling it," he said.
The bank said the sale should not be seen as a reduction of its activites in the region as it could lead to increased cooperation with Nicholas-Applegate.
Such co-operation might involve distribution of Nicholas-Applegate products, an industry source said.
The bank said Southeast Asia remained a "strategic priority" for Credit Lyonnais, particularly in merchant banking and capital market activities as well as in private banking.
CLIAM-Asia will take the name of Nicholas-Applegate Capital Management.
